documentation: GOLDEN.md (same directory) is normative; read it before porting.

grid16.order: row-major over rows x cols: k = i*16 + j -> array[rows[i]][cols[j]]

core16.order: row-major over rows x cols: k = i*16 + j -> array[rows[i]][cols[j]]

encodings.mask bits_b64: base64 of 2048 bytes; pixel p = y*128+x lives in byte p>>3 at bit p&7, LSB-first (bit 0 = value 1); 1 = transmissive. Same convention as ladder.bin.
encodings.phase float32_b64: base64 of 65536 bytes = 128*128 IEEE-754 binary32, little-endian, row-major (index = y*128 + x).

synthetic_predictor.gt: gt = mask * phase (the masked ground-truth wavefront, as in evaluate.py)
synthetic_predictor.note: No transcendental functions, so any IEEE-754 double implementation reproduces it bit-for-bit. The +0.3 constant is pure piston and MUST cancel in masked_piston_corrected_mse and in strehl_ratio's peak ratio.

reference_circle_psf.note: This peak is the divisor in simulate_measurement when normalize_by_peak=True.

phase_generation.rng: numpy Generator(PCG64) seeded 20260914; coeffs drawn in order phase0(cs=1.0), phase1(cs=1.0), phase2(cs=2.0), phase3(cs=2.0) as rng.uniform(-cs, cs, (1,33)). A JS port must NOT reproduce the RNG -- it takes coeffs_f64 as input.

noise_probe.purpose: Only path that distinguishes the operation ORDER inside simulate_measurement. Noiseless cases cannot: the circle divisor cancels against the final renorm.
noise_probe.recipe: psf = |FFT{P e^{i phi}}|^2 ; psf /= 1263376.0 ; psf = max(psf + sigma*noise, 0) ; psf /= max(psf.max(), 1e-6)

zernike_spot_checks.note: R_at_r = zernike_radial(n, |m|, r_probe); Z_at_r_theta = zernike(n, m, r_probe, theta_probe) elementwise.
